title: AFCE / AFFY / AF Gruppen / Atlas Financial / AFH Financial / Armstrong Flooring — Security, Reserve, Catalyst and Runway V9

notes: Raw Short -> actual Long corrections: AFCE 2012, AFFY 2016, AFHIF 2021.
AFHBL 2021 is not common equity; it is Atlas Financial Holdings 6.625% Senior Unsecured Notes due 2022, later exchanged into 6.625%/7.25% PIK Toggle Notes due 2027.
No source-DB horizon performance rows were found for these ten ideas; outcomes rely on SEC/company operating results, corporate actions, direct consideration and split-adjusted historical prices.
Atlas Financial executed a 1-for-3 reverse stock split in January 2013, so AFH 2012 entry $1.77 equals about $5.31 on a post-split basis.
AFHBL's 2022 exchange preserved face principal in new securities but this is not treated as realized par recovery. The new notes mature April 27, 2027, which is still in the future.
Atlas common and Atlas notes are judged separately. The 2024 transfer of core subsidiaries to a secured lender is a negative common and credit event.
AFH Financial Group's 480p cash acquisition consideration is used as the realized-value anchor for the 2020 Long.
Armstrong Flooring filed Chapter 11 on May 8, 2022 and later stated existing equity holders would likely receive no recovery after substantially all assets were sold.

meta.one_line_verdict_ko: 2012 EPS/SSS/unit growth가 적중하고 $16.50 entry가 2017 $79 cash deal로 약 4.8x
meta.key_mechanism: system sales, royalty economics and franchise-funded unit growth compounded earnings before strategic acquisition

meta.one_line_verdict_ko: 거대한 NOL face value에도 value-unlocking reverse merger가 장기간 현실화되지 않아 time-value 기준 실패
meta.key_mechanism: NOL value required profitable taxable income and a legally usable transaction, neither of which crystallized

meta.one_line_verdict_ko: backlog와 balance sheet quality는 유지됐지만 2024 revenue/margin 및 NOK248 target이 크게 미달
meta.key_mechanism: backlog did not convert into the growth and margin profile embedded in the starting valuation

batch_lessons: A turnaround that has already become a franchisor compounder should be underwritten on system sales, SSS, net openings and royalty economics rather than old asset-sale discounts.
NOL face value is not cash; monetization requires taxable income, legal usability and a timely catalyst.
A high-quality contractor can still be a poor stock if backlog converts at lower revenue and margins than assumed.
Reverse splits must be normalized before comparing historical entry and exit prices.
Specialty insurer book value is only as reliable as reserve adequacy.
Distressed exchanges should be marked to the market value of replacement securities rather than their face principal.
An asset-light MGA business can coexist with a highly levered holding-company security; enterprise quality and common-equity payoff must be separated.
Financial-buyer takeouts are useful external value anchors for recurring-revenue consolidators.
Spin-offs do not solve fixed-cost or cash-burn problems by themselves.
In distressed manufacturing turnarounds, liquidity runway must exceed time-to-normalized EBITDA.
